notes: encodePointerSegment escapes ~ and / only to build a JSON Pointer inside a human-readable Zod error string that is never parsed back, so no decode inverse is needed.
enqueueAdd pushes an ADJUST_STATE command into a CommandsManager whose process() drains the buffer (buffer.length = 0), so the dequeue inverse is owned by the runtime loop, not this producer.
enqueueFactAdjust enqueues an ADJUST_FACT command consumed by the CommandsManager process loop; the consuming/draining half is owned elsewhere.
enqueueMirroredFactAdjust merely composes two enqueueFactAdjust calls (run + permanent) into the same drained command buffer, so no separate inverse applies.
enqueueDragAssignment queues an ASSIGN_BODIES_BATCH into the runtime command buffer, and the drag_restore path in resolveDragReleaseUpdate already provides the logical undo.
enqueuePendingBodyHabitiUpdate queues an UPDATE_BODIES_BATCH command drained by the runtime command loop, so no producer-side dequeue is required.
enqueueCollectedCommands/enqueueAll forward already-collected commands into context.commandsManager which drains them, so the inverse lives in the processing loop.
enqueueInitialSpawn queues SPAWN commands into the runtime buffer; the KillHandler is the runtime-level inverse and is not this seed-helper's responsibility.
enqueueStateMutation just dispatches to ADD/SUB/SET enqueuers writing to the drained CommandBuffer, so the dequeue inverse is handled by the command processor.
enqueueSet pushes an UPDATE_STATE command into the CommandsManager buffer that is drained by process(), so no local inverse is needed.
enqueueSub enqueues an ADJUST_STATE with negative delta and enqueueAdd is its literal mirror in the same file, both drained by the command loop.
enqueueTraitUpdate queues an UPDATE_TRAITS_BATCH used by both executeAddTraitAction and executeRemoveTraitAction, and the buffer is drained by the runtime, so no separate inverse is missing.
pushVeinEdge appends to a rebuilt graph buffer that is fully cleared each frame via edges.length = 0 (VeinsSystem.ts:55, graphBuilderUtils.ts:18), so the bulk-clear inverse exists.
pushIncoming builds a fresh incomingByTarget index during a one-shot reference walk that is returned to the caller, so there is no removal lifecycle to mirror.
pushLever appends to a fresh local levers array constructed and returned by scan(), a build-once collection with no removal semantics.
serializePhysicsBody has its deserialize counterpart restorePhysicsBody in the same file (also syncPhysicsBody), so the mirror pair is present.
serializeDelaySignature is a one-way join(',') used only as a glyph-registry map key (GlyphRegistry.ts:104), never parsed back to an array, so no deserialize is needed.
serializeFlyweightEntity has its inverse hydrateFlyweightEntity defined in the same file, so the serialize/deserialize pair is complete.
